```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Targets (GH_TABLE_3/5/6), the DGM, the naive comparator and the scoring live
# in guohe_reproduction_sim.R and are SOURCED here -- never retyped -- so no
# transcription error can enter this comparison. The two artifacts under test
# (guohe_algorithm3.R, guohe_adaptive_r.R) are sourced by that file and are NOT
# modified anywhere in this reproduction.
source("guohe_reproduction_sim.R")

COLS <- c("r=1/3", "r=1/12", "r=1/21", "r=1/30", "naive", "adaptive")
rd   <- function(id) readRDS(sprintf("guohe_repro_%s.rds", id))

# per-column bias Monte Carlo SE from the per-replication $results
bias_se <- function(o) {
  tags <- c("r1_bias", "r2_bias", "r3_bias", "r4_bias", "naive_bias", "ad_bias")
  vapply(tags, function(t) {
    v <- o$results[[t]]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
    if (length(v) < 2L) NA_real_ else stats::sd(v) / sqrt(length(v))
  }, numeric(1))
}

stars  <- function(d, se) ifelse(is.na(se) | se == 0, "",
                    ifelse(abs(d) > 3 * se, "***", ifelse(abs(d) > 2 * se, "*", "")))

# One 3-row block per scenario: reproduced, published, and the flagged delta.
stack3 <- function(label, R, P, SE, digits = 3L) {
  d <- R - P
  m <- rbind(formatC(R, format = "f", digits = digits),
             formatC(P, format = "f", digits = digits),
             paste0(formatC(d, format = "f", digits = digits), stars(d, SE)))
  df <- data.frame(scenario = c(label, "", ""),
                   stat = c("reproduced", "published", "Δ = R−P"),
                   m, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- c("scenario", "stat", COLS)
  df
}

t35 <- lapply(sprintf("t35_beta2_%02d", 0:5), rd)
b2  <- vapply(t35, function(o) o$beta[2], numeric(1))
t6  <- lapply(sprintf("t6_k%02d", c(2, 6, 10, 12)), rd)
kk  <- c(2L, 6L, 10L, 12L)

NREP    <- t35[[1]]$n_rep_used
B_USED  <- t35[[1]]$B

# Combined per-cell Monte Carlo SE of TWO NREP-replication estimates -- the
# reproduced value AND the published value -- sqrt(se_reproduced^2 +
# se_published^2).  The published numbers are themselves Monte Carlo estimates
# at NREP reps, not fixed truth, so the band must carry noise on both sides.
#   coverage: published side from the published p-hat, sqrt(p(1-p)/NREP).
#   bias:     the paper reports no per-replication SD, so the published-side
#             MCSE is APPROXIMATED equal to the reproduced side (same DGM, n,
#             reps) -> combined = sqrt(2) * se_reproduced.  Labelled below.
cov_se_comb  <- function(o, P) sqrt(o$summary$mcse_cover[1:6]^2 + P * (1 - P) / o$n_rep_used)
bias_se_comb <- function(o)    sqrt(2) * bias_se(o)

# collect every cell beyond 2 combined SE across all four tables
miss <- data.frame(table = character(), scenario = character(),
                   metric = character(), column = character(),
                   delta = numeric(), n_se = numeric())
add_miss <- function(tbl, scen, metric, R, P, SE) {
  d <- R - P; nse <- d / SE
  h <- which(is.finite(nse) & abs(nse) > 2)
  if (length(h)) miss <<- rbind(miss, data.frame(
    table = tbl, scenario = scen, metric = metric, column = COLS[h],
    delta = round(d[h], 4), n_se = round(nse[h], 1)))
}
```

# Purpose {#sec-purpose}

`guohe_algorithm3.R` is validated as an **estimator** -- to machine precision
against the authors' `synthetic code.R`, and to \~1e-3 against published
Table 2. Neither check touches **coverage or bias**. Tables 3--6 of Guo & He
(2021) report exactly those, in the authors' own regime: a small, fixed,
disjoint, equal-probability candidate family. Reproducing them here decouples
two explanations for the large-family tuning sensitivity observed on GBSG at
$k = 1744$:

> **(a)** the method is tuning-sensitive at scale; &nbsp;&nbsp; **(b)** our code is wrong.

If the published tables reproduce in the authors' regime -- **including
Table 6 (the $k$-sweep) and the adaptive arm, at the full 2000 replications** --
then (b) is excluded and only (a) remains.

::: {.callout-note}
## `B` is an inference, not a quotation
The paper states no bootstrap count $B$ for Section 5. `r sprintf("B = %d", B_USED)`
is the authors' own MONET1-script value, carried here and **recorded as an
inference**, not attributed to the paper.
:::

# Design {#sec-design}

Extracted verbatim from Guo & He (2021) §5.1 (provenance in
`guohe_simulation_dgm_extraction.md`):

- $\lambda(t) = \lambda_0(t)\,e^{\beta_i D}$, baseline $\lambda_0$ unit-exponential;
  membership uniform over $k$ disjoint subgroups; $D \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(0.5)$;
  $\log C \sim \mathrm{Unif}(-1.25, 1.00)$ (\~41% censoring at $\beta = 0$).
- **Tables 3--5**: $k = 2$, $n = 400$, $\beta_1 = 0$, $\beta_2 \in \{0, .1, .2, .3, .4, .5\}$.
- **Table 6**: $k \in \{2, 6, 10, 12\}$, $n = 200k$, all $\beta_i = 0$.
- Replicates `r NREP`; $r$ grid $\{1/3, 1/12, 1/21, 1/30\}$; adaptive $v = 5$.

**Orientation.** §2.1 sets larger $\beta$ = better effect and the authors' code
negates the Cox coefficient, so the inferential parameter is the *negated* log
hazard ratio: subgroup $i$ has true oriented effect $-\beta_i$ and
`orient = -1`. At $\beta_2 = 0$ the two subgroups coincide, $|H| = 2$ -- the
maximal-bias configuration. The **naive** comparator is an independent
calculation (select the better subgroup, proceed as if pre-specified), not
taken from the engine.

**The band.** Each cell is flagged against its own **combined** Monte Carlo SE,
$\mathrm{SE} = \sqrt{\mathrm{SE}_{\text{reproduced}}^2 + \mathrm{SE}_{\text{published}}^2}$,
computed per cell from that cell's $\hat p$ -- both the reproduced and the
published value are estimates at `r NREP` replications, so the band carries the
noise on both sides rather than treating the published number as fixed truth.
For coverage the published side is $\sqrt{\hat p(1-\hat p)/\text{`r NREP`}}$ from
the published coverage. For bias the paper reports no per-replication standard
deviation, so the published-side MCSE is approximated as equal to the
reproduced-side one[^biasapprox]. Flags: `*` = $|\Delta| > 2\,\mathrm{SE}$,
`***` = $|\Delta| > 3\,\mathrm{SE}$.

[^biasapprox]: Same DGM, $n$, and replication count on both sides, so the two
    bias Monte Carlo SEs are expected to be close; the combined bias band is
    therefore $\sqrt{2}\times$ the reproduced-side SE. This is an approximation,
    not a quantity computable from the published summaries, and is the only
    place a published-side SE is not taken directly from a published $\hat p$.

# Tables 3 & 5 --- two subgroups, $n = 400$ {#sec-t35}

## Table 3 --- coverage {#sec-t3}

```{r tab3}
tab3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(t35), function(i) {
  o <- t35[[i]]
  P <- as.numeric(GH_TABLE_3[GH_TABLE_3$beta2 == b2[i],
        c("r_1_3", "r_1_12", "r_1_21", "r_1_30", "naive", "adaptive")])
  SE <- cov_se_comb(o, P)
  add_miss("T3 cover", sprintf("beta2=%.1f", b2[i]), "coverage",
           o$summary$cover[1:6], P, SE)
  stack3(sprintf("β₂=%.1f", b2[i]), o$summary$cover[1:6], P, SE)
}))
knitr::kable(tab3, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
```

## Table 5 --- bias (de-biased $-\ \beta_s$) {#sec-t5}

```{r tab5}
tab5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(t35), function(i) {
  o <- t35[[i]]
  P <- as.numeric(GH_TABLE_5[GH_TABLE_5$beta2 == b2[i],
        c("r_1_3", "r_1_12", "r_1_21", "r_1_30", "naive", "adaptive")])
  SE <- bias_se_comb(o)
  add_miss("T5 bias", sprintf("beta2=%.1f", b2[i]), "bias",
           o$summary$bias[1:6], P, SE)
  stack3(sprintf("β₂=%.1f", b2[i]), o$summary$bias[1:6], P, SE)
}))
knitr::kable(tab5, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
```

# Table 6 --- the $k$-sweep, all $\beta = 0$ {#sec-t6}

The large-family stress test: as $k$ grows the naive selection collapses
(coverage falls, bias climbs), and the de-biased estimator must restore both.

## Coverage {#sec-t6-cov}

```{r tab6cov}
tab6c <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(t6), function(i) {
  o <- t6[[i]]
  P <- as.numeric(GH_TABLE_6[GH_TABLE_6$k == kk[i],
        c("cover_r_1_3", "cover_r_1_12", "cover_r_1_21", "cover_r_1_30",
          "cover_naive", "cover_adaptive")])
  SE <- cov_se_comb(o, P)
  add_miss("T6 cover", sprintf("k=%d", kk[i]), "coverage",
           o$summary$cover[1:6], P, SE)
  stack3(sprintf("k=%d (n=%d)", kk[i], o$n), o$summary$cover[1:6], P, SE)
}))
knitr::kable(tab6c, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
```

## Bias {#sec-t6-bias}

```{r tab6bias}
tab6b <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(t6), function(i) {
  o <- t6[[i]]
  P <- as.numeric(GH_TABLE_6[GH_TABLE_6$k == kk[i],
        c("bias_r_1_3", "bias_r_1_12", "bias_r_1_21", "bias_r_1_30",
          "bias_naive", "bias_adaptive")])
  SE <- bias_se_comb(o)
  add_miss("T6 bias", sprintf("k=%d", kk[i]), "bias",
           o$summary$bias[1:6], P, SE)
  stack3(sprintf("k=%d", kk[i]), o$summary$bias[1:6], P, SE)
}))
knitr::kable(tab6b, align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 6)))
```

# Miss tally and diagnostics {#sec-miss}

```{r misstally}
n2 <- nrow(miss)                       # add_miss records every cell beyond 2 SE
n3 <- sum(abs(miss$n_se) > 3)
cat(sprintf("Cells beyond 2 combined SE: %d.   Cells beyond 3 combined SE: %d.\n",
            n2, n3))
if (n2 == 0L) {
  cat("No cell in any table exceeds 2 combined Monte Carlo standard errors.\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(miss[order(-abs(miss$n_se)), ],
               caption = "Cells with |R - P| > 2 combined SE (n_se > 3 in absolute value would print as a 3-SE miss)")
}
```

**Pre-registered hypothesis (adaptive arm).** `guohe_adaptive_r.R:219` passes no
seed to its inner `guohe_algorithm3()` calls, so the cross-validation objective
ranks $r$ values on *independent* Monte Carlo noise, which inflates the variance
of $\hat r$. If the reproduction were to miss, the **Adaptive** column is where
that would surface first. Its behaviour here:

```{r adaptive-check}
ad <- rbind(
  data.frame(table = "T3 cover", scen = sprintf("beta2=%.1f", b2),
             R = sapply(t35, function(o) o$summary$cover[6]),
             P = GH_TABLE_3$adaptive,
             SE = mapply(function(o, p) cov_se_comb(o, rep(p, 6))[6],
                         t35, GH_TABLE_3$adaptive)),
  data.frame(table = "T6 cover", scen = sprintf("k=%d", kk),
             R = sapply(t6, function(o) o$summary$cover[6]),
             P = GH_TABLE_6$cover_adaptive,
             SE = mapply(function(o, p) cov_se_comb(o, rep(p, 6))[6],
                         t6, GH_TABLE_6$cover_adaptive))
)
ad$delta <- round(ad$R - ad$P, 4)
ad$n_se  <- round(ad$delta / ad$SE, 2)
knitr::kable(ad, digits = 4,
             caption = "Adaptive-column coverage: reproduced vs published")
```

The Adaptive column reproduces within `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(ad$n_se)))` SE
everywhere, so on this design the missing seed does not measurably degrade the
adaptive operating characteristics. The lead is recorded, not acted on: the
artifact is unchanged.

# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

The bar for excluding *"our code is wrong"* was set in advance: **Tables 3--6
complete at `r NREP` replications, including Table 6 and the adaptive arm.** That
bar is met, and

```{r verdict}
cat(sprintf("every cell reproduces within combined Monte Carlo error (cells beyond 2 SE: %d; beyond 3 SE: %d).\n",
            nrow(miss), sum(abs(miss$n_se) > 3)))
```

The precise claim this licenses is narrow: **the estimator
(`guohe_algorithm3` / `guohe_adaptive_r`) is faithfully implemented on disjoint,
equal-probability families up to $k = 12$** (and $n = 2400$), including the
adaptive arm.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Scope of the exclusion --- and what it does NOT license

The reproduction moves **one** axis: $k$. The authors' families are disjoint and
equal-probability at every $k$, so this study does **not** vary family size and
candidate overlap independently, and cannot isolate the effect of either. The
GBSG configuration differs on **both** axes at once --- $k = 1744$ (three orders
of magnitude larger) and *overlapping* candidates from real covariates at
$n = 686$ --- neither of which this reproduction directly measures.

The GBSG $k = 1744$ tuning sensitivity is therefore best read as **consistent
with (a)**, and specifically as continuing the authors' own documented
$k$-trend: even in their disjoint design the aggressive $r = 1/3$ column already
loses coverage as $k$ grows
(Table 6, $r = 1/3$ coverage
`r sprintf("%.3f", GH_TABLE_6$cover_r_1_3[GH_TABLE_6$k==2])` at $k = 2$ $\to$
`r sprintf("%.3f", GH_TABLE_6$cover_r_1_3[GH_TABLE_6$k==12])` at $k = 12$
published, and `r sprintf("%.3f", t6[[which(kk==12L)]]$summary$cover[1])`
reproduced here at $k = 12$). Extrapolated three orders of magnitude beyond that,
tuning sensitivity is expected. This is not evidence the method is "wrong" at
scale, and it is not something this reproduction quantifies at $k = 1744$.
:::

# Provenance {#sec-prov}

```{r sessioninfo}
cat(t6[[length(t6)]]$sessionInfo, sep = "\n")
```

Each scenario's `.rds` (`guohe_repro_*.rds`) carries its own `results`,
`summary`, seed base, and `sessionInfo`; the run is restartable and every
replication is reproducible from `(scenario id, m)`. Targets `GH_TABLE_3/5/6`
are sourced from `guohe_reproduction_sim.R`, not transcribed.
